A1.justification: Both complete 20-page PDFs describe the same ADR framework and include Appendices A-D. Their text, equations, tables, and figures support reliable comparison; the appendices match in both text and rendered appearance.

before.justification: v1 reports original data-distribution analyses, ADR evaluations using LLaVA 1.5 and ShareGPT4V, tail-concept accuracy, and ablations, including detailed results in Appendix A.

after.justification: v3 retains these original analyses and experimental outcomes, including benchmark comparisons in Table 3, tail-concept results in Table 5, and appendix ablations.

M1.justification: Entity analysis, adaptive data rebalancing, language and ControlNet-based synthesis, and Appendix C's Algorithm 1 are unchanged. No method component or procedure is revised.

E1.justification: The training datasets, benchmark tasks, and tail-concept evaluation scenarios remain unchanged. Appendix A retains the same additional benchmark coverage and augmentation experiments.

E2.justification: Tables 3-4 retain the same base models and comparisons with EL2N, Perplexity, CLIP Score, and COINCIDE. Comparator membership in the appendix experiments is also unchanged.

E3.justification: Reported training-instance budgets, benchmark metrics, tail-subset construction, and fixed-data-volume ablation procedures are unchanged. No evaluation protocol or experimental setting is revised.

E4.justification: The perspective-combination and synthesis ablations, augmentation comparisons, failed-case analyses, and qualitative examples are retained unchanged. Figure 6's corrected caption does not change its underlying analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same point estimates and benchmark averages. Neither supplies repeated-run counts, random-seed information, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Numerical results, rankings, and qualitative examples are unchanged throughout the main text and appendices. Table 4 changes Ours-DR's SEED score from 61 to 61.0 and Ours' MMB score from 65 to 65.0, which are equivalent numerical formatting.

T1.justification: Entity definitions, reverse-indexed distributions, sampling probabilities, and the synthesis-count formula in Equation 1 are unchanged. No mathematical assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and applicability claims, including the claimed 4.36% relative average improvement over LLaVA 1.5 without increasing training-data volume.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning head-data redundancy, tail-data scarcity, and preservation of head performance are unchanged. The focus remains instruction tuning, with extension to pretraining still proposed as future work.

D1.justification: v3 adds a title-page project address displaying vlmlt.github.io, although its embedded hyperlink targets prmbench.github.io. Implementation details, pseudocode, prompts, and existing resource links in Appendices B-D are unchanged; the PDFs do not establish a new code or data release.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, research positioning, and all 71 cited works remain unchanged. Reference 27's citation-page backlink changes only because introduction text moves from page 1 to page 2.

P1.justification: Localized edits update an author email, add the project-page line, and correct Figure 6's caption wording. The narrative, section organization, and appendix text remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The added title-page line causes limited reflow of Figure 1 and introduction text. Figure 6's caption changes from 'data rebalancing synthesis methods' to 'data synthesis methods,' and Table 4 standardizes two decimal displays. No figures or tables are added or removed.

improvement.justification: The scientific contribution and supporting evidence are unchanged. Correcting Figure 6's caption provides a small clarity benefit, but the new project link has conflicting displayed and target addresses. The PDFs cannot establish whether this pointer improves resource access or misdirects readers, leaving the net quality effect of these limited changes uncertain.
